solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sets out with currency that's been converted?

parts.note: something that has been converted is no longer what it was, a former thing, so ex-
pounds sterling are the British currency

explanation.surface: Someone lays out their money that has been exchanged into another currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: pounds that have been converted are no longer pounds, so they are ex-pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain or set forth an argument in detail.

clue.text: Finally, time is up, by clock

indicators.note: Finally, placed at the start, applies to each of the following four words, taking the last letter of each

explanation.surface: Someone notices the clock showing that time has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is a verb here, informal British for noticing or spotting something.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock someone is slang for catching sight of them, the same as to spot.

clue.text: Sweet Dot given fresh flower

parts.note: to dot or sprinkle a surface with things is to pepper it
mint condition is fresh and new
the flower of something is its finest part, the cream

explanation.surface: A woman called Dot is handed a newly picked bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name and 'flower' like a bloom; they are the verb pepper and the best part, cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint cream is a fondant confection flavoured with mint, a kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Madness, having uranium near each child

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
EA is the abbreviation for each, as on price lists
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Insanity blamed on living close to radioactive material for every child.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is the absence of reason, an irrational state of mind akin to insanity.

clue.text: Dropped off note and final letter

parts.note: do (or doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale
zed is the British name of Z, the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone delivered a message and a last letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped off' suggests delivering post, but means fell asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep, which is to have a brief nap.

clue.text: Pimp linking minister to a parliamentarian

parts.note: REV, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A procurer connecting a churchman with a politician, a scandal story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pimp' is the modern slang verb, as in pimping a car: doing it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pimp something, informally, is to make it showier, the same as giving it a makeover.

clue.text: Did second check in English dictionary

indicators.note: in says the check sits inside the English dictionary letters

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone double-checked a word in an English dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did second' means seconded a view by repeating it, not timed something.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone's words is to repeat or second them, agreeing aloud.

clue.text: Summons requesting company to go to court?

definitions.text: Summons requesting company to go to court?

parts.words: Summons requesting company to go to court?
parts.note: a summons sounds legal, but this is a jolly invitation for a partner to play on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A legal summons demanding a firm attend court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' is friends, not a firm, and 'court' a tennis court, not a law court: the stock phrase from old drawing-room comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is a cheery invitation for someone to join a game on the courts.

clue.text: Fine strike that's spotted in football field

parts.note: a fine is a penalty for an offence
to box someone's ears is to strike them

explanation.surface: A fine imposed after a strike, with something spotted on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' is apt: the penalty spot lies inside the area.
explanation.definitionFit: The penalty area on a soccer pitch contains the penalty spot, so it is literally spotted.

clue.text: See books covering county's missing years?

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see

indicators.note: covering says the books wrap around the county

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: Look at books about a county's lost years.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucestershire is an English county in the west; its abbreviation is the standard postal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-lost relative or friend has been absent for many years, unseen and untraced.

clue.text: Twice a year kid meets old cameraman

indicators.note: Twice says the abbreviation for a year is written two times

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for a year
to kid or tease someone is to razz them, an Americanism

explanation.surface: A child meets an elderly photographer twice yearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A paparazzo is one of the celebrity-chasing press photographers, the singular of paparazzi.

clue.text: Back in Normandy: a Hungarian composer

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words Normandy: a Hungarian

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Hungarian composer returns to Normandy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is the signal that the letters are concealed in the phrase. Haydn was Austrian, though he served the Hungarian Esterhazy princes.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian composer known as the father of the symphony.

clue.text: First light sees one charmed by swan

indicators.note: First says the light comes at the front, ahead of the one

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: At dawn a woman is bewitched by a swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First light' looks like dawn; 'First' only places the light before the one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Zeus took the form of a swan to seduce the Spartan queen, mother of Helen.

clue.text: Possible place for setter's cryptic legend on back of book

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so these letters are jumbled
back of takes the final letter of book

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's puzzling caption printed on the back cover of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is not the crossword compiler but the dog breed, as in an Irish setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel is a hutch where a hound such as a setter might sleep.

clue.text: Repeatedly cold, this most unconventionally fine shower!

indicators.note: unconventionally means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
Repeatedly says the cold abbreviation is used twice

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a very cold, odd drizzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is CC plus THIS MOST, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch mist is a thick drizzling fog of very fine rain typical of the Highlands.

clue.text: Mormon wandering in valley briefly finds place of rest

indicators.note: in places the jumbled Mormon inside the shortened valley
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a coomb or combe is a short valley in England

indicators.note: wandering means straying, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: A wandering Mormon finds somewhere to rest in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: MMONRO, the jumble of Mormon, goes inside COOM (coomb less its B).
explanation.definitionFit: A common room is a lounge in a college or school where staff or students relax.

clue.text: Fixing undiluted drink, suddenly left, upset

parts.note: raw spirit is undiluted

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to gulp is to drink quickly in one go

explanation.surface: Someone downs neat spirit, leaves quickly and is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GULP plus L into LPLUG. Rawlplug is a British trade name for a wall plug.
explanation.definitionFit: This brand of wall plug is a fixing for screws in masonry.

clue.text: Dodgy moment, not the first

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a very short time

explanation.surface: A shady moment, not the first of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or suspect, the same as questionable.

clue.text: Moan endlessly about tablets for hearing and breathing problem?

indicators.note: about says the shortened moan wraps around the tablets
endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to whinge is British slang for to moan or complain

indicators.note: for hearing says the tablets are given by their sound, written phonetically

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so tablets are Es

explanation.surface: Someone complains constantly about tablets for a hearing or breathing problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for hearing' looks medical but marks the sound: Es said aloud gives EEZ, set inside WHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing with a whistling rattle is a symptom of asthma, a breathing complaint.

clue.text: Colour dry clothing with it

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the dry letters enclose the fashionable word

parts.note: TT means teetotal, and a dry person does not drink
in means fashionable, like with it

explanation.surface: Dye clothes while staying trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or hue, a light colouring.

clue.text: Sudden change for American humorist into small red jumper

indicators.note: into puts the humorist inside the other letters

parts.note: Che Guevara is the classic red, a revolutionary communist
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
a wit is a humorist

explanation.surface: An American comedian squeezes into a small red sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for sweater, but here it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Switcheroo is American slang for an unexpected reversal or swap.

clue.text: Neat, I agree

definitions.meaning: said to confirm something is exactly right

explanation.surface: Someone approves a tidy result.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exactly so, used both of tidy arrangement and as assent.

clue.text: Was glitchy volume increased on a good day?

indicators.note: on says the following letters come after the greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting, like saying good day
cc, cubic centimetres, measures volume
upped means raised or increased

explanation.surface: A sound system acting up when the volume was turned up on a nice day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good day' is not the weather but a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor glitch, so a system that hiccupped had a brief malfunction.

clue.text: Government department do: couple in the end have left

indicators.text: couple in the end have left
indicators.note: the last two letters, a couple at the end, are taken away

parts.note: to do someone is slang to cheat or defraud them

explanation.surface: A government event where the last pair of guests have gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party; it is the verb, to swindle. DEFRA is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the abbreviated name of a British ministry, a state department.

clue.text: Always apparently packing an extra five in a single square container

indicators.text: apparently packing an extra five in a single square
indicators.note: V is five in Roman numerals; squeeze a second V into the same grid square and it looks like a W, a double V

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A puzzle about cramming a pentagonal extra into one grid cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Vs side by side resemble the letter W, so doubling the five within one square changes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Capital letters, initially and finally, turning up in ciphers

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters between the two zeros

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, written O

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading upwards, so backwards
initially and finally take the first and last letters of letters

explanation.surface: Capitals appearing at the start and end of coded messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital letters' reads as upper case; 'Capital' is the definition. The first and last of letters, L and S, turn to SL between two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Logo for channel that is reversing its polarity?

indicators.note: reversing polarity swaps the poles, so south becomes north

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's emblem that flips its magnetic poles.
explanation.walkthrough: S and N are the compass abbreviations for south and north.
explanation.definitionFit: In television, an ident is the short logo sequence identifying the station between programmes.

clue.text: Rude Finns could make enemies

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be reworked into another word

explanation.surface: Ill-mannered Scandinavians might turn people against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rude' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfriend is an old word for a foe or adversary, so the plural means foes.

clue.text: Feisty female to play Doctor Who, at last, enters

indicators.note: enters means goes inside the playing word

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of Who

explanation.surface: A spirited woman lands the role of the Doctor in Doctor Who.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' is a long-running BBC sci-fi series; here the words split into MB and the last letter of Who.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboy is a girl who enjoys rough, boisterous activities, typically spirited and bold.

clue.text: True stories about river fronts producing algae

indicators.note: fronts means stands in front of, so the stories with the river come before the true word
about says the stories wrap around the river

parts.note: sagas are long stories
so means true, as in is that so

explanation.surface: Factual accounts about a river's banks and what grows there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river fronts' looks like riverbanks; 'fronts' instead places the stories before 'True'. The Sargasso Sea is named after this floating weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso is a floating brown seaweed, gulfweed, a kind of marine alga.
